about.title: Ukiah Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Mendocino County residents rely on a small number of local hospitals and clinics for care, which means when something goes wrong medically in Ukiah, the ripple effects can be significant for a patient and their family. Medical malpractice cases are different from car crash claims — they hinge on whether a provider deviated from the accepted standard of care, not simply on a bad result. California's MICRA framework adds specific procedural steps, including an early notice requirement and firm deadlines, that make prompt action important. If you believe a delayed diagnosis, medication error, surgical mistake, or birth injury happened at a Ukiah-area facility, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who evaluates these cases regularly. There's no cost to find out where you stand, and no obligation to move forward. Getting informed early, while records and details are still fresh, can make a real difference in how a claim is built.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Pursue a Claim

items.title: Strict Filing Windows Apply
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the injury, and no more than three years from when it occurred. Waiting to explore your options can shrink the time available to build a case.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a lawsuit can be filed, California law typically requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider or facility. An attorney familiar with this step can help make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is generally required to show the care fell below an accepted standard — a bad outcome by itself isn't enough. Connecting with an attorney who can arrange this kind of review is a key early step.

items.question: Is every bad medical result considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor outcome alone doesn't prove negligence. A claim generally requires showing a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and that this caused the harm. An independent attorney can help assess whether your situation meets that bar.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after care I received in Ukiah?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened, whichever comes first. Because Ukiah patients sometimes travel to nearby counties for specialized treatment, it's worth clarifying where and when the care occurred. An attorney can help pin down the applicable deadline for your specific facts.

items.question: Does California limit what I can recover in a malpractice case?
items.answer: Yes, California's MICRA law places a cap on non-economic damages, though that cap is set to rise annually under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally handled separately. An independent attorney can walk through how these rules might apply to your situation.
